key_insight: GaDiT generates disordered atomic structures and enables interpretable inverse design targeting structural features, physical properties and preparation conditions.
engineering_relevance: The framework could accelerate exploration of amorphous materials by linking controllable atomic disorder to desired material properties.
method: Combines a diffusion transformer with dynamic periodic graphs.
Uses masked conditioning and an interval-weighted training-noise distribution.
Applies conditioned atomic response mapping to identify relevant global descriptors and local atomic environments.
evidence_signal: Across 2D amorphous carbon and 3D amorphous silicon and silica, the abstract reports high-quality generation, roughly 100× faster sampling than existing corrector-based approaches and inverse design beyond training-distribution structure–property ranges.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify validation protocols or computational costs, leaving physical reliability beyond the training distribution and practical speedups to be assessed.
paper_title: Graph diffusion transformer for interpretable generation and inverse design of disordered atomic structures
